extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/prosecutors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making and documenting statutory and nonstatutory (obviousness-type) double patenting rejections, provisional rejections, and related procedural actions (terminal disclaimers, rejoinder of claims, transitional restriction rules) in Office actions under pre‑AIA and AIA/FITF regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common-ownership / relatedness conditions for double patenting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a double patenting rejection when the reference patent/application and the application under examination satisfy one or more relationship conditions: (a) name the same inventive entity, (b) name different inventive entities but are commonly assigned, (c) are not commonly assigned but name at least one joint inventor in common, (d) are filed by a common applicant (35 U.S.C. 118), (e) claim patentably indistinct inventions made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of a joint research agreement (pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c)) for pre‑AIA cases, or (f) claim patentably indistinct inventions and were commonly owned or deemed commonly owned as of the effective filing date under applicable AIA/FITF provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This a–f list appears repeatedly and is the baseline test for whether various double patenting form paragraphs may be used. When applicable, additional form paragraphs (e.g., 8.27.fti/8.27.aia or 8.28.fti/8.28.aia) may also be required to resolve priority/common‑ownership evidence. Always consider whether the time of common ownership (effective filing date) matters (especially under AIA/FITF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional statutory double patenting rejection (¶ 8.32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a provisional statutory double patenting rejection where claim [1] is provisionally rejected as claiming the same invention as claim [2] of a copending Application No. [3] (reference application) — i.e., the scope of the claimed inventions is identical and the identical claims have not been patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements and notes: form paragraph 8.30 must precede this paragraph; do not use if the identical claims are in an issued patent (use 8.31 instead); do not use for nonstatutory double patenting; applicable relationship conditions (a–f) must be checked; use 8.28.fti/8.28.aia as appropriate to require assignee to name first inventor or to resolve ownership; if record evidence shows pre‑AIA 102(f)/(g) prior art, also make rejections using 7.15.fti/7.19.fti; under FITF/AIA, use 8.27.aia as appropriate and consider a 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for nonstatutory double patenting (¶ 8.33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonstatutory double patenting is a judicially created doctrine to prevent unjustified timewise extension of the patent 'right to exclude' and harassment by multiple assignees. It is appropriate where conflicting claims are not identical but at least one claim is not patentably distinct from the reference claim(s) because it is anticipated by or would have been obvious over the reference claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting nonstatutory (obviousness‑type) double patenting, an obviousness analysis is required only if the examined claim(s) are not anticipated by the reference claim(s). A timely filed terminal disclaimer in compliance with 37 C.F.R. 1.321(c)/(d) (and signed per 1.321(b)) may overcome the rejection if the reference is commonly owned or the invention arose under a joint research agreement. Examiner should cite MPEP §§ 717.02 and 706.02(l)(1)-(3) (AIA vs non‑AIA distinctions). USPTO eTerminal Disclaimer procedures/forms may be used (auto‑processing if all requirements met).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of heading form paragraph 8.33
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 8.33 is to be used as a heading before any nonstatutory double patenting rejection using form paragraphs 8.34–8.39.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 8.33 must precede any of form paragraphs 8.34–8.39 and must be used only ONCE in an Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting rejection — patent primary reference, no secondary references (¶ 8.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claim [2] of U.S. Patent No. [3]. Although claims are not identical, they are not patentably distinct because [4].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph for ODP rejections based on a patent (not on an application). Insert the patent number in bracket 3 and, in bracket 4, provide an explanation for anticipation or a rationale for obviousness of the examined claims over the reference claims. If evidence indicates the patent is prior art under pre‑AIA 102(f)/(g), also make a 103(a) rejection using form paragraph 7.21.fti when applicable. Under FITF/AIA also consider 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) or 103 rejections if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting rejection — copending application primary reference, no secondary references (¶ 8.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provisionally rejected as unpatentable over claim [2] of copending Application No. [3] because, though not identical, the claims are not patentably distinct because [4]. This is provisional since the indistinct claims have not been patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this when the indistinct claims are in another copending application (not a patent). Form paragraph 8.33 must precede this paragraph. Insert reference application number in bracket 3 and explain anticipation/obviousness in bracket 4. If the reference application is commonly assigned now but does not show common ownership at the time of invention, also use 8.28.fti to resolve priority/ownership issues. Consider additional pre‑AIA 102(e)/103(a) rejections (form paragraphs 7.21.01.fti/7.21.02.fti) where earlier‑filed disclosures support a statutory rejection. Under FITF/AIA, also make 102(a)(2) or 103 rejections as appropriate. See MPEP §1490 for terminal disclaimer guidance and note that 35 U.S.C. 119(a)/(e) benefit/priority claims are not considered in double‑patenting earlier‑filed determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting — patent primary reference with secondary references (¶ 8.36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] rejected as unpatentable over claim [2] of U.S. Patent No. [3] in view of [4]; [5].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph when making an ODP rejection that relies on a patent primary reference plus secondary reference(s) (i.e., an obviousness‑type analysis). Insert patent number in bracket 3, secondary reference in bracket 4, and explain the obviousness analysis in bracket 5. If the primary patent may be prior art under pre‑AIA 102(f)/(g), consider an additional pre‑AIA 103(a) rejection (form paragraph 7.21.fti). Under pre‑AIA, if the primary patent issued to a different inventive entity and has an earlier effective filing date, consider 102(e)/103(a) rejections (form paragraph 7.21.02.fti). For FITF/AIA, also consider 102(a)(2) or 103 rejections if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional nonstatutory double patenting — copending primary application with secondary references (¶ 8.37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim [1] provisionally rejected as unpatentable over claim [2] of copending Application No. [3] in view of [4]; [5]. This is provisional because the patentably indistinct claims have not been patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where the primary reference is a copending application and an obviousness analysis with secondary references is needed. Insert primary ref application number in bracket 3, secondary reference in bracket 4, and the obviousness rationale in bracket 5. If the primary reference is commonly assigned now but common ownership at the time of invention is not established, use 8.28.fti in addition. For FITF/AIA, use 8.28.aia if the primary reference is to a different inventive entity but commonly assigned and there is no evidence of common ownership as of the effective filing date. Consider additional pre‑AIA 102(e)/103(a) rejections where appropriate (7.21.01.fti).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonstatutory double patenting based solely on improper timewise extension (In re Schneller) — with patent (¶ 8.38) and with another application (¶ 8.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a nonstatutory double patenting rejection asserting that allowance of the claims would improperly extend the 'right to exclude' already granted in an issued patent or would improperly extend rights of a copending application, where the subject matter claimed in the instant application is fully disclosed in and covered by at least one claim of the patent or the copending application (and there is no apparent reason the applicant was prevented from presenting corresponding claims earlier).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only with TC Director approval when relying on In re Schneller. For patents: use only when the patent is commonly owned or there is at least one joint inventor/common applicant; insert patent number and describe the common subject matter in bracket 4. For copending applications: ensure common ownership/joint inventor/common applicant and insert reference application number and description of subject matter. If record indicates pre‑AIA 102(f)/(g) issues, also make pre‑AIA 103(a) rejections as appropriate. For FITF/AIA, consider 102(a)(2)/103 rejections if appropriate. See MPEP §804 and In re Schneller authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional restriction / election of species requirement — pre‑GATT filing (¶ 8.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark an application subject to transitional restriction provisions of Public Law 103‑465 (effective June 8, 1995) when: (1) application filed on or before June 8, 1995, and (2) has an effective U.S. filing date of June 8, 1992 or earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in restriction/election of species requirements for applications subject to 37 C.F.R. 1.129(b). Not applicable to design or reissue applications. Inform applicant of their options: elect the invention(s) to be searched/examined and pay fee under 37 C.F.R. 1.17(s) for each additional independent distinct invention, or file a petition under 37 C.F.R. 1.129(b). Reference Federal Register and Official Gazette notices for final rules and current fee schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable product — rejoinder of at least one process claim, less than all claims (¶ 8.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim directed to an allowable product is present, a process claim (claim [2]) previously withdrawn due to a restriction requirement may be rejoined and examined if the process claim requires all the limitations of the allowable product claim; other claims not rejoined must not include all limitations of the allowable product claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP §821.04(b) and 37 C.F.R. 1.104. Insert the allowable product claim number(s) and rejoined process claim numbers in the indicated brackets; specify which claims are not rejoined and the subject matter of those claims. Withdrawal of the restriction requirement is effected as to the rejoined inventions; once withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 no longer applies (see In re Ziegler). Warn applicant that continuation/divisional claims that are anticipated by or include all limitations of an allowable claim may be subject to provisional double patenting rejections over the instant application's claims. If ALL previously withdrawn process claims are being rejoined, use form paragraph 8.43 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable product — rejoinder of all previously withdrawn process claims (¶ 8.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claim ([1]) directed to an allowable product is present, and ALL process claims previously withdrawn from consideration are being rejoined, those process claims ([2]) are rejoined and fully examined under 37 C.F.R. 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph (not 8.42) when all previously withdrawn process claims are rejoined. State the allowable product claim number(s), the process claim numbers, and note that the restriction requirement from the prior Office action is withdrawn; once withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 no longer applies. If rejoinder occurs after the first Office action on the merits and rejoined claims are unpatentable (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 112(a) rejection), the next Office action may be final if appropriate under MPEP §706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected invention allowable — rejoinder of all previously withdrawn claims (¶ 8.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an elected invention (claim [1]) is allowable and other claims ([2]) previously withdrawn for restriction require all the limitations of an allowable claim, the restriction requirement is withdrawn and the previously withdrawn claims are rejoined and fully examined under 37 C.F.R. 1.104.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP §821.04(a) procedures. If the elected invention is a product and previously nonelected process claims are rejoined, use 8.43 instead. Insert bracketed information as directed. Warn applicants that, as with other rejoinders, continuation/divisional claims could be subject to provisional double patenting rejections over allowable claims of the present application. Once the restriction is withdrawn, 35 U.S.C. 121 is no longer applicable.
